reasons: No tests are visible for this file.
The dark-mode fonts depend on an outside service with no fallback described.
The startup listener is added and never removed.

terms.meaning: A small amount of data the browser keeps between visits.
A React function that gives a component shared state it can read.
A marker written onto a page element that style rules can check.
A file of style rules, here fonts, loaded from a website.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for theme handling
sections.what: Brings in the React helper that lets components read changing shared values.
sections.why: Likely reason: the theme is shared state that many components read.

sections.name: Theme, listeners
sections.title: Light or dark theme choice
sections.what: Defines the two theme options, light (the default) and dark (opt-in), the storage key name, and the list of components waiting for theme changes.
sections.why: Likely reason: light is the original look and dark is an optional mode stored per browser.
sections.watch_out: Renaming the storage key makes every visitor's saved choice reset to light.

sections.name: read
sections.title: Reading the saved theme
sections.what: Reads the theme saved in the browser and defaults to light if nothing is saved or storage is blocked. Also sets the starting theme value and the address of the dark-mode font stylesheet.
sections.why: Likely reason: the saved choice should persist between visits, and light is the safe fallback.
sections.watch_out: If storage is blocked, as in some private browsing modes, the choice lasts only for the current page load.

sections.name: loadDarkFonts
sections.title: Loading dark-mode fonts on demand
sections.what: Adds the dark-mode font stylesheet to the page the first time dark mode is used, and never adds it twice.
sections.why: The code comment says light pages fetch nothing extra.
sections.watch_out: The check depends on a fixed element id, so changing that id could add the stylesheet more than once.

sections.name: apply
sections.title: Applying the theme to the page
sections.what: Marks the page's root element for dark styling, or removes the mark for light, and tells the browser which color scheme to use for built-in controls such as scrollbars.
sections.why: Likely reason: the style rules switch on one marker, so one change restyles the whole page.
sections.watch_out: Dark-mode style rules depend on this exact marker, so renaming it breaks dark mode without an error.

sections.name: initTheme
sections.title: Setting the theme before first paint
sections.what: Runs once at startup. A link with a theme setting in its web address can choose and save a theme. It then applies the current theme and listens for changes made in other browser tabs.
sections.why: The code comment says this runs before the first render so the wrong theme never flashes on screen.
sections.watch_out: Each call adds another storage listener and none are removed, so calling this more than once duplicates the work.

sections.name: setTheme
sections.title: Switching the theme on request
sections.what: Saves the chosen theme, applies it to the page, and notifies every component that shows the theme so they update together.
sections.why: Likely reason: one entry point for theme switches keeps the saved and shown themes in step.
sections.watch_out: If saving fails because storage is blocked, the theme still changes for this visit only, and the visitor may think it was saved.

sections.name: useTheme, useIsDark
sections.title: Letting components read the theme
sections.what: Gives a component the current theme or a yes or no for dark mode, and updates it when the theme changes. On the server, light is assumed.
sections.why: Likely reason: the React mechanism for shared values that change outside React's normal flow.
sections.watch_out: Only components that use these hooks update on a change; a component reading the theme another way will stay stale.

sections.name: prefersReducedMotion
sections.title: Checking the reduced-motion setting
sections.what: Returns true when the visitor's operating system asks for less motion.
sections.why: Likely reason: so animations can be skipped for people who are sensitive to motion.
sections.watch_out: It can return an empty value in some cases, so use it as a plain true or false check rather than comparing it strictly.

summary: Stores and applies the light or dark theme, and tells the components that show it when it changes.
purpose: Lets a visitor choose a dark look that is remembered in their browser, with light as the default.
why: The code comment says light is the original design and stays untouched, while dark is an opt-in choice stored per browser.
how: 1. At startup, reads a theme from the web address or from saved browser storage. 2. Marks the page for dark styling and loads dark fonts when needed. 3. Watches for theme changes made in other browser tabs. 4. When the visitor switches theme, it saves the choice, applies it and notifies the components.
inputs: The saved theme in browser storage, a theme setting in the web address, theme switches from the page, and changes made in other tabs.
outputs: A marker on the page's root element, a font stylesheet when dark mode loads, and the current theme for each component.
risks: Dark mode fetches fonts from an outside Google address, so a visitor's browser contacts a third party. A shared link with a theme setting can permanently change the visitor's saved theme. Calling the startup function twice adds duplicate listeners.
debug: If dark mode does not stick, check that the browser allows saved storage. If dark fonts do not load, check that the outside font address can be reached. If one tab does not follow another, check the storage change listener. If the page flashes the wrong theme, check when the startup function runs.
